eberron.institution.prince-oargev.blocked_reason: An authority entry needs no special effect.

eberron.institution.kaius-iii.name: Kaius III

effect.summary: Karrnath’s king who rejected the Blood of Vol and disbanded the orders.

eberron.institution.kaius-iii.go_wrong: Rebellious Emerald Claw members refused to surrender.
eberron.institution.kaius-iii.combines: His policy caused the order to fragment.
eberron.institution.kaius-iii.blocked_reason: A ruler entry needs no special effect.

eberron.institution.gold-dragon-inns.name: Gold Dragon Inns

effect.summary: A chain of inns offers standardized traveler lodging and services.

eberron.institution.gold-dragon-inns.cost_or_limit: Services and prices are standardized; room counts and amenities vary.
eberron.institution.gold-dragon-inns.who_may: Travelers; buildings accommodate halfling-sized and taller guests.
eberron.institution.gold-dragon-inns.where_from: Operated by House Ghallanda across Khorvaire.
eberron.institution.gold-dragon-inns.combines: House Thuranni and House Phiarlan provide licensed entertainers at most inns.
eberron.institution.gold-dragon-inns.blocked_reason: This is an organization, not a game effect.

effect.summary: A group of rowdy Brelish veterans with no larger criminal affiliation.

eberron.institution.little-fingers.name: Little Fingers

effect.summary: Pickpockets and cutpurses who pay a tithe to the Boromars and avoid designated targets.

eberron.institution.little-fingers.combines: Loosely allied with the Boromar Clan.

effect.summary: Khoravar half-elves who frequently assault and disfigure elves.
Changeling pickpockets working in Middle Menthis.
Gnomes and halflings who specialize in illusion magic.

eberron.institution.the-mourners.name: The Mourners

effect.summary: Cyran veterans presenting themselves as a militia protecting Cyran refugees.

eberron.institution.the-mourners.cost_or_limit: Some may be pursuing selfish interests.

effect.summary: Bugbears who claim to protect Malleon’s Gate and have recently aligned with Daask.

eberron.institution.the-quiet-folk.name: The Quiet Folk

effect.summary: Goblins who avoid violence and use stealth and sewer knowledge for theft.

eberron.institution.the-quiet-folk.combines: Stealth and knowledge of the sewers

effect.summary: Mostly shifters and half-orcs who live in Menthis sewers and defend their territory.
A publication presented with an editorial about aberrant marks.

eberron.institution.the-dark-six.name: The Dark Six

effect.summary: A religious group whose priests Daask brought to Sharn.

eberron.institution.the-dark-six.combines: Daask restored a temple to the Six in Khyber’s Gate.

eberron.institution.the-sharn-watch.name: The Sharn Watch

effect.summary: Sharn’s law-enforcement organization, sometimes bribed or intimidated by criminal groups.

eberron.institution.the-sharn-watch.go_wrong: Officers may take bribes, look the other way, or be coerced.
eberron.institution.the-sharn-watch.combines: Has dealings with the Boromar Clan and Daask.

eberron.institution.the-blackened-book.name: The Blackened Book

effect.summary: An elite group of abjurers and diviners investigating and containing magical threats.

eberron.institution.the-blackened-book.cost_or_limit: Acts only on missions assigned by superiors.
eberron.institution.the-blackened-book.go_wrong: A politically inconvenient case may not be assigned.

eberron.institution.guardians-of-the-gat.name: Guardians of the Gate

effect.summary: A division monitoring foreign nationals and immigrants, especially in High Walls.

eberron.institution.guardians-of-the-gat.go_wrong: May use unnecessary violence against refugees.
eberron.institution.guardians-of-the-gat.combines: Has a civilian branch for administration and customs investigations.

eberron.institution.the-redcloak-battali.name: The Redcloak Battalion

effect.summary: An elite force called in when extreme military force is needed.

eberron.institution.the-redcloak-battali.cost_or_limit: Acts only when mustered by a Watch captain.
eberron.institution.the-redcloak-battali.go_wrong: Typically not deployed when action is against Boromar interests.

eberron.institution.gatekeeper-druids.name: Gatekeeper druids

effect.summary: Closed portals to Xoriat and crafted seals to hold the daelkyr at bay.

eberron.institution.gatekeeper-druids.cost_or_limit: The protection lasts while the seals remain intact.
eberron.institution.gatekeeper-druids.go_wrong: If the seals fail, the daelkyr may rise.
eberron.institution.gatekeeper-druids.combines: Their seals constrain Xoriat’s power and the daelkyr.
eberron.institution.gatekeeper-druids.blocked_reason: The lasting containment depends on seals and a condition for their failure.

eberron.institution.karrnathi-army.name: Karrnathi army

effect.summary: Maintains undead soldiers in its service.

eberron.institution.karrnathi-army.cost_or_limit: Some undead are sealed in vaults; others remain in service.
eberron.institution.karrnathi-army.go_wrong: Soldiers may be turned against the living, a concern raised by Karrns.
eberron.institution.karrnathi-army.mind: Undead soldiers can make tactical decisions under the Odakyr Rites.
eberron.institution.karrnathi-army.combines: Uses Karrnathi undead soldiers created through the Odakyr Rites.

eberron.institution.house-vol.name: House Vol

effect.summary: Elven line that practiced necromancy and bore the Mark of Death.

eberron.institution.house-vol.cost_or_limit: The line was targeted for extermination.
eberron.institution.house-vol.go_wrong: Its heirs were hunted and its mark was sought for elimination.
eberron.institution.house-vol.combines: Its heir Erandis became Lady Illmarrow.

eberron.institution.cannith-creation-for.name: Cannith creation forges

effect.summary: none

eberron.institution.cannith-creation-for.combines: Associated with the possible origin of the Lord of Blades.
eberron.institution.cannith-creation-for.blocked_reason: This is an institution, not a game effect.

eberron.institution.generic-npcs.name: Generic NPCs

effect.summary: A section heading introducing customizable nonplayer character examples.

eberron.institution.generic-npcs.blocked_reason: This is a section heading, not an institution.

eberron.institution.lady-illmarrow.name: Lady Illmarrow

effect.summary: A leader served by surviving bone knights of the Emerald Claw.

eberron.institution.lady-illmarrow.combines: Associated with the Order of the Emerald Claw.
eberron.institution.lady-illmarrow.blocked_reason: A named leader is not an organization or a special effect.

effect.summary: none
none
none

eberron.institution.sixty-families.name: Sixty Families

effect.summary: none

eberron.institution.sixty-families.cost_or_limit: standing invitations to the Tain Gala

eberron.rule.dragonmarks-grant-limited-m.name: Dragonmarks grant limited magical abilities

effect.summary: Hereditary dragonmarks give some family members useful trade-related magic.

eberron.rule.dragonmarks-grant-limited-m.cost_or_limit: The abilities are limited and appear only in certain family members.
eberron.rule.dragonmarks-grant-limited-m.who_may: People in dragonmarked families who manifest a mark.
eberron.rule.dragonmarks-grant-limited-m.combines: Dragonshards can make marks more powerful.
eberron.rule.dragonmarks-grant-limited-m.blocked_reason: The passage states a limited magical capability but no unsupported mechanics are needed.

eberron.rule.the-mourning.name: The Mourning

effect.summary: A mist engulfed Cyre and horribly transformed what it caught; the cause remains unknown.

eberron.rule.the-mourning.cost_or_limit: The passage gives no known cause, range limit, or way to prevent it.
eberron.rule.the-mourning.go_wrong: A nation was devastated and over a million people died.
eberron.rule.the-mourning.combines: Possible causes include war magic, Cannith research, or a released Overlord; none is confirmed.
eberron.rule.the-mourning.blocked_reason: The broad, persistent mist effect transforms targets across a region, beyond the basic target grammar.

eberron.rule.draconic-prophecy.name: Draconic Prophecy

effect.summary: Signs reveal conditional possible futures, and fulfilling their conditions can shape history.

eberron.rule.draconic-prophecy.cost_or_limit: It presents possibilities rather than a single inevitable future; interpretation can vary.
eberron.rule.draconic-prophecy.go_wrong: Misinterpretation or fulfillment of a condition can lead to major consequences.
eberron.rule.draconic-prophecy.mind: Readers must contemplate and interpret signs.
eberron.rule.draconic-prophecy.who_may: Those able to read the signs; long-studying dragons, fiends, and scholars are prominent students.
eberron.rule.draconic-prophecy.where_from: Patterns and signs scattered across the world
eberron.rule.draconic-prophecy.combines: Conjunctions, moons, symbols, and ancient inscriptions

eberron.rule.warforged-aging.name: Warforged aging

effect.summary: Warforged show no known age-related deterioration and resist magical aging.

eberron.rule.warforged-aging.blocked_reason: This lifespan restriction can be handled as an ordinary immunity rule.

eberron.rule.dragonmark-inheritance-and-.name: Dragonmark inheritance and manifestation

effect.summary: Marks arise in certain bloodlines and usually appear around adolescence, but many heirs never manifest one.

eberron.rule.dragonmark-inheritance-and-.cost_or_limit: About half of members of a bloodline manifest a mark.
eberron.rule.dragonmark-inheritance-and-.combines: The Test of Siberys places heirs in circumstances likely to provoke manifestation.
eberron.rule.dragonmark-inheritance-and-.blocked_reason: This is a setting constraint that can be applied as a character-generation rule.

eberron.rule.korth-edicts.name: Korth Edicts

effect.summary: The dragonmarked houses are required to maintain political neutrality; house-agent papers support cross-border travel on house business.

eberron.rule.korth-edicts.cost_or_limit: Applies to the dragonmarked houses and their political alignment.
eberron.rule.korth-edicts.combines: House papers can be used to claim authorized travel across national borders.

eberron.rule.dragonmark-appearance-and-p.name: Dragonmark appearance and persistence

effect.summary: A mark warms, may glow without useful illumination, and can grow in size and complexity as its bearer develops.

eberron.rule.dragonmark-appearance-and-p.cost_or_limit: A mark cannot be removed; if its marked limb is severed, it eventually appears elsewhere on the bearer.
eberron.rule.dragonmark-appearance-and-p.combines: Appearance may vary and can include quirks.
eberron.rule.dragonmark-appearance-and-p.blocked_reason: The mark is an inseparable, persistent power-bearing feature of the body.

eberron.rule.infusion-learning-limits.name: Infusion learning limits

effect.summary: An infusion with a minimum level cannot be learned before that level, and normally cannot be learned more than once.

eberron.rule.infusion-learning-limits.cost_or_limit: The infusion description may state exceptions.
eberron.rule.infusion-learning-limits.combines: Replicate Magic Item expressly permits repeated learning.
eberron.rule.infusion-learning-limits.blocked_reason: This is a simple character-option restriction.

eberron.rule.eldritch-cannon-limit.name: Eldritch Cannon limit

effect.summary: An artificer normally has one cannon, cannot create another while one remains, and needs a rest or spell slot to create one again.

eberron.rule.eldritch-cannon-limit.cost_or_limit: One cannon at a time; creation refreshes on a long rest or costs a spell slot; the cannon ends at 0 hit points or after one hour.
eberron.rule.eldritch-cannon-limit.go_wrong: The cannon disappears when destroyed or expired.
eberron.rule.eldritch-cannon-limit.combines: At 15th level, the maximum becomes two.
eberron.rule.eldritch-cannon-limit.blocked_reason: The rule governs a powered object’s capacity, persistence, and creation cost.

eberron.rule.steel-defender-replacement-.name: Steel Defender replacement and revival

effect.summary: A dead defender can be revived within an hour using tools and a spell slot; creating a replacement destroys the former defender, and its creator’s death ends it.

eberron.rule.steel-defender-replacement-.cost_or_limit: Revival takes one minute and costs a spell slot of at least 1st level; replacement requires a long rest and smith’s tools.
eberron.rule.steel-defender-replacement-.go_wrong: The defender perishes if its creator dies or a new one replaces it.
eberron.rule.steel-defender-replacement-.blocked_reason: The rule models a persistent companion with independent life, death, and restoration.

eberron.rule.homunculus-disappearance.name: Homunculus disappearance

effect.summary: The homunculus vanishes if it or its creator dies, leaving its heart behind.

eberron.rule.homunculus-disappearance.cost_or_limit: The infused gem or crystal remains as the heart.
eberron.rule.homunculus-disappearance.go_wrong: Death causes disappearance rather than ordinary continued existence.
eberron.rule.homunculus-disappearance.blocked_reason: This requires special companion death and persistent-object rules.

eberron.rule.replicable-item-eligibility.name: Replicable item eligibility

effect.summary: Replicate Magic Item selects from level-gated lists or eligible common items, excluding potions and scrolls.

eberron.rule.replicable-item-eligibility.cost_or_limit: The chosen list is restricted by artificer level; each use of the infusion selects an item.
eberron.rule.replicable-item-eligibility.combines: Item attunement requirements are indicated by the table.
eberron.rule.replicable-item-eligibility.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward eligibility restriction.

eberron.rule.prophecy-fulfillment-can-ta.name: Prophecy fulfillment can take different forms

effect.summary: A prophetic passage can be fulfilled in different ways, potentially more than once over centuries.

eberron.rule.prophecy-fulfillment-can-ta.cost_or_limit: Interpretations are notoriously difficult and may be multiple.
eberron.rule.prophecy-fulfillment-can-ta.combines: Characters may attempt to steer a fulfillment.

eberron.rule.xen-drik-exploration-author.name: Xen’drik exploration authorization

effect.summary: University explorers need letters of marque from Breland’s king to explore Xen’drik ruins.

eberron.rule.xen-drik-exploration-author.go_wrong: Exploration without the required papers lacks the stated permission.
eberron.rule.xen-drik-exploration-author.combines: University documentation may secure the papers.
eberron.rule.xen-drik-exploration-author.blocked_reason: This is a permission restriction that can be represented as a game-world rule.

eberron.rule.darguun-treaty-law.name: Darguun treaty law

effect.summary: Darguun does not follow the common laws of the treaty nations, and enforcement is unpredictable.

eberron.rule.darguun-treaty-law.cost_or_limit: Local customs and clan authority govern daily life.
eberron.rule.darguun-treaty-law.go_wrong: Conduct treated as criminal elsewhere may be ordinary here.

eberron.rule.slavery-in-rhukaan-draal.name: Slavery in Rhukaan Draal

effect.summary: Haruuc abolished slavery in the capital, though some clan lords still practice it elsewhere.

eberron.rule.slavery-in-rhukaan-draal.cost_or_limit: The abolition is geographically limited in practice.
eberron.rule.slavery-in-rhukaan-draal.go_wrong: Clan lords may continue slavery outside the capital.

eberron.rule.the-laws-of-karrnath.name: The laws of Karrnath

effect.summary: Karrnath imposes unusually harsh laws and swift punishments.

eberron.rule.the-laws-of-karrnath.cost_or_limit: Luxury and excess are restricted; rationing continues
eberron.rule.the-laws-of-karrnath.blocked_reason: This is a setting rule rather than a character power.

eberron.rule.rationing-in-karrnath.name: Rationing in Karrnath

effect.summary: Ongoing rationing preserves supplies against future hardship.

eberron.rule.rationing-in-karrnath.cost_or_limit: The populace accepts limits on luxury goods and excess
eberron.rule.rationing-in-karrnath.blocked_reason: The rule specifies a society-wide supply limit.

eberron.rule.manifest-zones-and-lingerin.name: Manifest zones and lingering ghosts

effect.summary: Talenta zones linked to Dolurrh make ghosts more likely to linger.

eberron.rule.manifest-zones-and-lingerin.blocked_reason: The passage does not define the rules by which ghosts linger or depart.

eberron.rule.thrane-s-theocratic-authori.name: Thrane’s theocratic authority

effect.summary: The church holds ultimate authority while the queen serves in a symbolic advisory role.

eberron.rule.thrane-s-theocratic-authori.go_wrong: Political rule may distract the church and invite corruption.
eberron.rule.thrane-s-theocratic-authori.combines: The Keeper leads the state with practical assistance from the Council of Cardinals.
eberron.rule.thrane-s-theocratic-authori.blocked_reason: This is a political setting rule, not a supernatural effect.

eberron.rule.thronehold-restricted-groun.name: Thronehold restricted grounds

effect.summary: Thronehold Castle and its grounds are off limits and watched by the wardens.

eberron.rule.thronehold-restricted-groun.who_may: Throne Wardens guard the restricted area.
eberron.rule.thronehold-restricted-groun.blocked_reason: The restriction can be represented as a basic block on movement.

eberron.rule.patron-ancestor-bond-and-im.name: Patron ancestor bond and immortality

effect.summary: A Valenar elf may be recognized through a bond to a patron ancestor and gain a chance at immortality.

eberron.rule.patron-ancestor-bond-and-im.cost_or_limit: Recognition and a bond are prerequisites; immortality is only a possibility.
eberron.rule.patron-ancestor-bond-and-im.who_may: A half-elf with Valenar blood may aspire to the bond.
eberron.rule.patron-ancestor-bond-and-im.combines: Associated with the Keepers of the Past.
eberron.rule.patron-ancestor-bond-and-im.blocked_reason: The passage connects an ancestor bond to a chance at immortality without defining a playable soul-state mechanism.

eberron.rule.aereni-deathless-sustenance.name: Aereni deathless sustenance

effect.summary: Positive energy and descendants’ freely given devotion sustain Aerenal’s deathless.

eberron.rule.aereni-deathless-sustenance.cost_or_limit: Sustenance comes from Irian’s light and willingly given devotion.
eberron.rule.aereni-deathless-sustenance.go_wrong: Negative-energy necromancy is despised by Aereni society.
eberron.rule.aereni-deathless-sustenance.combines: Draws on Irian and descendant devotion, not Mabar.
eberron.rule.aereni-deathless-sustenance.blocked_reason: The mechanism sustains beings after death and relies on a defined soul-state.

eberron.rule.aerenal-negative-energy-pro.name: Aerenal negative-energy prohibition

effect.summary: Aereni reject necromancy drawing on Mabar’s negative energy.

eberron.rule.aerenal-negative-energy-pro.cost_or_limit: This is a cultural rejection and a mandate for the Undying Court’s agents.
eberron.rule.aerenal-negative-energy-pro.go_wrong: Such undead are treated as threats to destroy.
eberron.rule.aerenal-negative-energy-pro.who_may: Aereni society and Undying Court agents.
eberron.rule.aerenal-negative-energy-pro.blocked_reason: The passage states a cultural prohibition rather than a new supernatural effect.

eberron.rule.khyber-demiplane-connection.name: Khyber demiplane connections

effect.summary: A passage can lead through a demiplane and emerge far away, without following natural geography.

eberron.rule.khyber-demiplane-connection.cost_or_limit: Such connections are rare and stable once found.
eberron.rule.khyber-demiplane-connection.go_wrong: A newly opened or uncovered passage can release threats.
eberron.rule.khyber-demiplane-connection.combines: Portals may connect locations on opposite sides of the world.
eberron.rule.khyber-demiplane-connection.blocked_reason: The passage links distant locations through a nonlocal route, beyond ordinary movement effects.

eberron.rule.riedran-foreign-entry.name: Riedran foreign entry

effect.summary: Foreigners may enter Riedra legally only through Dar Jin and generally need a transit visa to go beyond the foreign quarter.

eberron.rule.riedran-foreign-entry.cost_or_limit: Few transit visas are granted; travelers must make a compelling case or evade the watch.

eberron.rule.ritual-body-warping-pacts.name: Ritual body-warping pacts

effect.summary: Mystical rituals and pacts warped bodies and produced the first changelings, skulks, and tiefling bloodlines.

eberron.rule.ritual-body-warping-pacts.cost_or_limit: Requires mystical rituals and pacts; further limits are unstated.
eberron.rule.ritual-body-warping-pacts.blocked_reason: The passage describes lasting bodily transformation, beyond the basic effect grammar’s supported operations.

eberron.rule.aureon-s-lawlessness-curse.name: Aureon’s lawlessness curse

effect.summary: Aureon’s curse leaves Xen’drik’s creatures without knowledge of law.

eberron.rule.aureon-s-lawlessness-curse.combines: One of the curses placed on Xen’drik.

eberron.rule.boldrei-s-city-curse.name: Boldrei’s city curse

effect.summary: Boldrei’s curse prevents cities from enduring; growing cities may collapse into madness.

eberron.rule.boldrei-s-city-curse.cost_or_limit: Affects cities; the passage says large cities may collapse.
eberron.rule.boldrei-s-city-curse.go_wrong: Cities that grow too large may collapse into madness.
eberron.rule.boldrei-s-city-curse.mind: May induce madness as a city fails.
eberron.rule.boldrei-s-city-curse.combines: One of the curses laid on the land.
eberron.rule.boldrei-s-city-curse.blocked_reason: The curse causes broad, persistent consequences and a possible madness outcome beyond the basic effect grammar.

eberron.rule.the-traveler-s-curse.name: The Traveler’s Curse

effect.summary: It distorts space so paths do not reliably lead to the same place.

eberron.rule.the-traveler-s-curse.cost_or_limit: Repeated travel along the same path may lead to different locations.
eberron.rule.the-traveler-s-curse.go_wrong: Explorers can become lost or fail to find a known site again.
eberron.rule.the-traveler-s-curse.combines: One of the curses laid on the land.

eberron.rule.the-devourer-s-fire-and-sto.name: The Devourer’s fire and storm

effect.summary: The curse brings fire and storms to Xen’drik.

eberron.rule.the-devourer-s-fire-and-sto.combines: One of the curses laid on the land.
eberron.rule.the-devourer-s-fire-and-sto.blocked_reason: The passage describes large-scale and unpredictable environmental effects.

eberron.rule.the-silver-flame-binds-the-.name: The Silver Flame binds the overlord

effect.summary: Tira’s sacrifice joined her spirit to the Flame and bound the escaped demon again.

eberron.rule.the-silver-flame-binds-the-.cost_or_limit: Requires Tira’s self-sacrifice and spirit union.
eberron.rule.the-silver-flame-binds-the-.go_wrong: The bound demon still yearns to mislead good people.
eberron.rule.the-silver-flame-binds-the-.mind: The lingering demon can tempt people toward evil.
eberron.rule.the-silver-flame-binds-the-.who_may: The Silver Flame through Tira Miron
eberron.rule.the-silver-flame-binds-the-.combines: Tira’s spirit is joined with the Silver Flame.
eberron.rule.the-silver-flame-binds-the-.blocked_reason: It describes a lasting supernatural prison for a powerful being, beyond a simple binding effect.

eberron.rule.only-elves-can-be-revenants.name: Only elves can be revenants

effect.summary: The Keepers hold that only elves can serve as revenants because half-elves cannot enter the needed trance.

eberron.rule.only-elves-can-be-revenants.cost_or_limit: Excludes half-elves under the Keepers’ teaching.

eberron.rule.undying-preservation.name: Undying preservation

effect.summary: The wisest and most accomplished elves are preserved after death as members of the Undying Court rather than being lost to Dolurrh.

eberron.rule.undying-preservation.cost_or_limit: Reserved for the wisest and most accomplished elves; living devotion sustains the Court.
eberron.rule.undying-preservation.who_may: Aereni elves who meet the Court’s standard
eberron.rule.undying-preservation.combines: The Court’s power is sustained by living elves’ devotion.
eberron.rule.undying-preservation.blocked_reason: Preserving the dead as continuing members of a court requires a soul-state and afterlife mechanism.

eberron.rule.major-bridge-feather-fall.name: Major-bridge feather fall

effect.summary: Major bridges in upper and middle wards automatically use feather fall to soften a fall.

eberron.rule.major-bridge-feather-fall.cost_or_limit: Applies to major bridges in upper and middle wards.
eberron.rule.major-bridge-feather-fall.go_wrong: Other bridges may leave a falling person to hit hard.

eberron.rule.six-stones-contest-outcome.name: Six Stones contest outcome

effect.summary: A Six Stones match ends when six of seven contestants are turned to stone; the last survivor wins most of the stakes.

eberron.rule.six-stones-contest-outcome.cost_or_limit: A portion of the stakes goes to the organizers; contestants carry no arms or armor and cannot use magic or attack the cockatrice.
eberron.rule.six-stones-contest-outcome.go_wrong: Contestants can be petrified or killed.
eberron.rule.six-stones-contest-outcome.blocked_reason: The contest depends on petrification, an unsupported form transformation.

eberron.rule.travel-time-between-sharn-w.name: Travel time between Sharn wards

effect.summary: none stated

eberron.rule.travel-time-between-sharn-w.cost_or_limit: Crossing a ward takes at least 30 minutes; add 30 minutes per ward passed; Dura and Tavick’s Landing double travel time within them.
eberron.rule.travel-time-between-sharn-w.combines: Travel by foot; bridges and ward routes affect journeys.
eberron.rule.travel-time-between-sharn-w.blocked_reason: This is a travel guideline rather than a world-effect rule.

eberron.rule.black-arch-enchanted-gates.name: Black Arch enchanted gates

effect.summary: In times of trouble, gates and checkpoints can make Black Arch impassable.

eberron.rule.black-arch-enchanted-gates.cost_or_limit: Usually open; may close during emergencies.
eberron.rule.black-arch-enchanted-gates.combines: Enchanted gates and checkpoints form the defense.
eberron.rule.black-arch-enchanted-gates.blocked_reason: An area-wide, conditional barrier is not represented by the basic effect grammar.

eberron.rule.high-walls-gates.name: High Walls gates

effect.summary: The Sharn Watch can seal the camp gates at any time.

eberron.rule.high-walls-gates.go_wrong: Residents may be trapped if the gates are sealed.
eberron.rule.high-walls-gates.blocked_reason: This rule concerns closing an area boundary, which requires an area-field effect.

eberron.rule.fallen-s-destruction.name: Fallen’s destruction

effect.summary: A floating tower crashed into the district, leading to its abandonment.

eberron.rule.fallen-s-destruction.go_wrong: The impact ruined and displaced the district’s inhabitants.
eberron.rule.fallen-s-destruction.blocked_reason: The passage describes an area-wide catastrophic impact beyond a simple targeted effect.

eberron.rule.solidified-clouds-support-s.name: Solidified clouds support Skyway

effect.summary: A floating island of solidified clouds supports a district above Sharn.

eberron.rule.solidified-clouds-support-s.combines: The district is built atop the cloud island.

eberron.rule.weapon-license-in-upper-tav.name: Weapon license in Upper Tavick’s Landing

effect.summary: Carrying a weapon requires a paid license issued after pleading one’s case.

eberron.rule.weapon-license-in-upper-tav.cost_or_limit: Costs 5 gp; unauthorized weapons may be confiscated.
eberron.rule.weapon-license-in-upper-tav.who_may: People carrying weapons in the ward.
eberron.rule.weapon-license-in-upper-tav.where_from: Upper Tavick’s Landing courthouse in Twelve Pillars district.
eberron.rule.weapon-license-in-upper-tav.combines: Blademarks and Watch officers can demand to see the license.

eberron.rule.spellcasting-license-in-upp.name: Spellcasting license in Upper Tavick’s Landing

effect.summary: Casting spells requires a paid license listing the intended spells.

eberron.rule.spellcasting-license-in-upp.cost_or_limit: Costs 10 gp; unauthorized magic can draw a fine.
eberron.rule.spellcasting-license-in-upp.who_may: People casting spells in the ward.
eberron.rule.spellcasting-license-in-upp.where_from: Upper Tavick’s Landing courthouse in Twelve Pillars district.
eberron.rule.spellcasting-license-in-upp.combines: The license specifies spells the user plans to cast.

eberron.rule.dress-law-in-upper-tavick-s.name: Dress law in Upper Tavick’s Landing

effect.summary: People must dress in a way officials consider suitable to the ward’s dignity.

eberron.rule.dress-law-in-upper-tavick-s.cost_or_limit: Armor is usually disallowed except for specified military or Deneith ties.
eberron.rule.dress-law-in-upper-tavick-s.go_wrong: Officials can escort violators from the ward.
eberron.rule.dress-law-in-upper-tavick-s.combines: Interpretation rests with Blademarks and Watch officers.

eberron.rule.unruly-behavior-in-upper-ta.name: Unruly behavior in Upper Tavick’s Landing

effect.summary: Fighting, street shouting, and similar disruption can be punished.

eberron.rule.unruly-behavior-in-upper-ta.cost_or_limit: Fine up to 5 gp and temporary expulsion.
eberron.rule.unruly-behavior-in-upper-ta.go_wrong: Violators risk a fine and expulsion.

eberron.rule.old-sharn-portals-are-seale.name: Old Sharn portals are sealed

effect.summary: Metal and magic gates keep passages into Old Sharn closed, and tampering with them is illegal.

eberron.rule.old-sharn-portals-are-seale.go_wrong: Breaking the seals may expose the city’s hazards.
eberron.rule.old-sharn-portals-are-seale.combines: The gates were ordered sealed by King Galifar I.
eberron.rule.old-sharn-portals-are-seale.blocked_reason: Maintaining sealed portals is a containment effect outside the basic grammar.

eberron.rule.identity-theft-is-illegal.name: Identity theft is illegal

effect.summary: The law prohibits malicious theft of identity, including harmful impersonation by shapeshifting or illusion.

eberron.rule.identity-theft-is-illegal.cost_or_limit: Intent to cause harm is specified.
eberron.rule.identity-theft-is-illegal.combines: Includes shapeshifting and illusion used to impersonate another person.

eberron.rule.gambling-and-prostitution-r.name: Gambling and prostitution regulation

effect.summary: Gambling and prostitution are legal but heavily taxed and regulated.

eberron.rule.gambling-and-prostitution-r.go_wrong: Operating outside the rules risks legal trouble.

eberron.rule.dreamlily-is-a-heavily-taxe.name: Dreamlily is a heavily taxed good

effect.summary: Smuggled goods include dreamlily, which is heavily taxed.

eberron.rule.dreamlily-is-a-heavily-taxe.cost_or_limit: Taxation makes it a smuggling target.
eberron.rule.dreamlily-is-a-heavily-taxe.go_wrong: Smuggling or dealing in illegal goods risks prosecution.

eberron.rule.minor-crime-fines.name: Minor-crime fines

effect.summary: Officers may impose fines immediately for minor offenses.

eberron.rule.minor-crime-fines.cost_or_limit: Fine depends on the offense and may be increased by a magistrate.
eberron.rule.minor-crime-fines.combines: Possessions may be confiscated instead of gold.

eberron.rule.serious-offense-detention.name: Serious-offense detention

effect.summary: Serious offenders are held at a garrison pending trial; serious flight risks go to the Citadel headquarters.

eberron.rule.serious-offense-detention.cost_or_limit: A magistrate generally reviews the case within 1d4 days.
eberron.rule.serious-offense-detention.combines: A truth spell may be used in the magistrate’s review.

eberron.rule.sharn-criminal-punishments.name: Sharn criminal punishments

effect.summary: Fines are typical; alternatives include labor or service, branding, exile, magical punishment, and sometimes execution or imprisonment.

eberron.rule.sharn-criminal-punishments.cost_or_limit: Long imprisonment is unusual; it is reserved for cases where death would cause diplomatic harm.
eberron.rule.sharn-criminal-punishments.go_wrong: An outlaw loses legal protection and may be attacked without legal reprisal.
eberron.rule.sharn-criminal-punishments.combines: An unaffordable fine may become labor or special service.

eberron.rule.treaty-of-thronehold-creati.name: Treaty of Thronehold creation-forge restriction

effect.summary: The treaty required House Cannith to dismantle the forges that produced warforged.

eberron.rule.treaty-of-thronehold-creati.cost_or_limit: Creation forges producing warforged had to be dismantled.
eberron.rule.treaty-of-thronehold-creati.combines: Applies to House Cannith’s warforged-producing forges.
eberron.rule.treaty-of-thronehold-creati.mechanism: legal restriction on a production method

eberron.rule.planar-observatory-site-bal.name: Planar observatory site balance

effect.summary: An observatory must occupy a location balanced between Siberys and Khyber.

eberron.rule.planar-observatory-site-bal.cost_or_limit: Finding a suitable location may require years of surveying.

eberron.rule.dream-formation.name: Dream formation

effect.summary: All dreams occur in Dal Quor, where a sleeping mind shapes a shard of the plane, usually from its memories and emotions.

eberron.rule.dream-formation.cost_or_limit: Dreams are normally shaped by the dreamer’s own memories and emotions.
eberron.rule.dream-formation.go_wrong: Outside influence can make the dream sinister.
eberron.rule.dream-formation.mind: Dreams reflect the dreamer’s memories and emotions.
eberron.rule.dream-formation.combines: Outside effects such as the dream spell can influence dreams.
eberron.rule.dream-formation.blocked_reason: The rule involves shaping a dream from mental content and external alteration of that content.

eberron.rule.death-in-dreams.name: Death in dreams

effect.summary: A dream figment simply disappears; an actually dreaming character who dies gains no rest benefit and takes 3d6 psychic damage.

eberron.rule.death-in-dreams.cost_or_limit: Applies differently to dream figments and actual dreamers.
eberron.rule.death-in-dreams.go_wrong: A quori may trap the dreamer in Dal Quor while possessing their body.
eberron.rule.death-in-dreams.mind: Dream death can leave the character trapped in a nightmare.
eberron.rule.death-in-dreams.combines: Quori possession may create a more severe outcome.
eberron.rule.death-in-dreams.blocked_reason: The possible separation of a dreamer from their possessed body involves a persistent mind or soul state.

eberron.rule.dream-communication.name: Dream communication

effect.summary: Dreaming Dark agents can communicate and coordinate in dreams without exposing their cover.

eberron.rule.dream-communication.combines: Supports covert assignment and information transfer.
eberron.rule.dream-communication.blocked_reason: Communication through shared or influenced dreams requires a mental channel beyond the basic grammar.

eberron.rule.warlord-claim-to-rule.name: Warlord claim to rule

effect.summary: A creature commanding a loyal band and holding territory may call itself a warlord.

eberron.rule.warlord-claim-to-rule.cost_or_limit: Must command a band’s loyalty and successfully claim and hold territory.
eberron.rule.warlord-claim-to-rule.combines: Only a few warlords hold significant power.

eberron.rule.gatekeeper-seal-binding.name: Gatekeeper seal binding

effect.summary: Some seals keep particular daelkyr imprisoned in Khyber and weaken their powers.

eberron.rule.gatekeeper-seal-binding.cost_or_limit: Seals require their binding to remain intact; one bloodline seal lasts only while its final member lives.
eberron.rule.gatekeeper-seal-binding.go_wrong: A cracked or failing seal may allow influence or danger to spread.
eberron.rule.gatekeeper-seal-binding.combines: Seals may target specific daelkyr or ward more generally against aberrations and Xoriat.
eberron.rule.gatekeeper-seal-binding.blocked_reason: The rule concerns imprisonment and suppression of a powerful being, beyond basic effects.

eberron.rule.bloodline-seal-duration.name: Bloodline seal duration

effect.summary: A bloodline seal remains effective until the last member of the line dies.

eberron.rule.bloodline-seal-duration.cost_or_limit: The seal depends on at least one living bloodline member.
eberron.rule.bloodline-seal-duration.go_wrong: The binding ends when the line is extinguished.
eberron.rule.bloodline-seal-duration.blocked_reason: The passage specifies a magical binding whose continued existence depends on a living bloodline.

eberron.rule.seal-reenergizing-ritual.name: Seal reenergizing ritual

effect.summary: An annual ritual can reenergize a seal and keep it shut for another year.

eberron.rule.seal-reenergizing-ritual.go_wrong: If not maintained, the seal may fail.
eberron.rule.seal-reenergizing-ritual.blocked_reason: The ritual renews a site-wide planar barrier, an area-field effect.

eberron.rule.gatekeeper-spirit-in-a-livi.name: Gatekeeper spirit in a living body

effect.summary: A long-dead Gatekeeper’s spirit can persist in the body of an ancient toad.

eberron.rule.gatekeeper-spirit-in-a-livi.cost_or_limit: The passage gives no duration or conditions.
eberron.rule.gatekeeper-spirit-in-a-livi.mind: The spirit speaks through the host body.
eberron.rule.gatekeeper-spirit-in-a-livi.combines: The host is an ancient toad.
eberron.rule.gatekeeper-spirit-in-a-livi.blocked_reason: A deceased person’s spirit continuing in a host body is a soul-state mechanic.

eberron.rule.last-war-ended-by-the-mourn.name: Last War ended by the Mourning

effect.summary: The Last War stopped after the Mourning destroyed Cyre, because people feared continuing the conflict could cause another catastrophe.

eberron.rule.last-war-ended-by-the-mourn.cost_or_limit: The cause of the Mourning is uncertain.
eberron.rule.last-war-ended-by-the-mourn.go_wrong: Continuing the war was believed to risk further cataclysm.
eberron.rule.last-war-ended-by-the-mourn.mind: Fear of the Mourning drove people to stop fighting.
eberron.rule.last-war-ended-by-the-mourn.who_may: The nations and leaders of Khorvaire
eberron.rule.last-war-ended-by-the-mourn.combines: The war ended without a victor or settled grievances.

eberron.rule.treaty-of-thronehold.name: Treaty of Thronehold

effect.summary: A treaty that recognizes Droaam’s status and ratifies Thrane’s occupation of Thaliost.

eberron.rule.treaty-of-thronehold.cost_or_limit: It also bars treaty-breaking raids and forbids Karrnath from creating new undead soldiers.
eberron.rule.treaty-of-thronehold.combines: Accepted by the nations described as parties to it.
eberron.rule.treaty-of-thronehold.blocked_reason: Its stated restrictions can be represented as ordinary game rules.

eberron.rule.the-mourning-and-renewed-wa.name: The Mourning and renewed war

effect.summary: Fear that another full-scale war could cause total destruction restrains the nations.

eberron.rule.the-mourning-and-renewed-wa.cost_or_limit: The restraint rests on fear of repeating the Mourning, not merely on treaty terms.
eberron.rule.the-mourning-and-renewed-wa.go_wrong: Renewed full-scale conflict risks utter destruction.
eberron.rule.the-mourning-and-renewed-wa.mind: Creates widespread fear of renewed war.
eberron.rule.the-mourning-and-renewed-wa.where_from: The unexplained cataclysm called the Mourning.
eberron.rule.the-mourning-and-renewed-wa.combines: The Mourning’s cause is unknown and may involve a controllable power.
eberron.rule.the-mourning-and-renewed-wa.blocked_reason: The constraint can be represented as a setting-level risk and motivation.

eberron.rule.every-fiend-spawned-from-kh.name: Every fiend spawned from Khyber owes fealty to one of these overlords.

effect.summary: Khyber-born fiends are obligated to serve an overlord.

eberron.rule.every-fiend-spawned-from-kh.cost_or_limit: The passage states this as a general obligation.
eberron.rule.every-fiend-spawned-from-kh.combines: Each Lords of Dust cabal serves a particular overlord.
eberron.rule.every-fiend-spawned-from-kh.blocked_reason: The obligation can be represented as a relationship or setting rule.

eberron.rule.mournland-arcane-energies.name: Mournland arcane energies

effect.summary: Lingering arcane energy can cause arbitrary bizarre magical effects.

eberron.rule.mournland-arcane-energies.where_from: The Day of Mourning and the remains of Cyre.
eberron.rule.mournland-arcane-energies.combines: Can alter land, creatures, and magic.
eberron.rule.mournland-arcane-energies.blocked_reason: The passage allows arbitrary effects across areas, beyond one basic effect target.

eberron.rule.mournland-provisions.name: Mournland provisions

effect.summary: Explorers must bring supplies or risk consuming contaminated food and water.

eberron.rule.mournland-provisions.cost_or_limit: Local food and water may be tainted.
eberron.rule.mournland-provisions.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward restriction on resource use.

eberron.rule.mournland-terrain-transform.name: Mournland terrain transformation

effect.summary: The Mourning raised land, swallowed lakes, moved cities, and turned terrain into glass or sludge.

eberron.rule.mournland-terrain-transform.go_wrong: The resulting terrain may be dangerous or impassable.
eberron.rule.mournland-terrain-transform.combines: Some plants and trees became stone-like materials.
eberron.rule.mournland-terrain-transform.blocked_reason: The changes transform large areas and many things at once.

eberron.rule.colossus-crew-requirement.name: Colossus crew requirement

effect.summary: Best operation requires marked captain, weapons officer, and helmsman; self-direction is possible but weaker.

eberron.rule.colossus-crew-requirement.cost_or_limit: Optimal roles require Marks of Making, Storm, and Passage respectively.
eberron.rule.colossus-crew-requirement.go_wrong: Without the full crew, power is diminished.
eberron.rule.colossus-crew-requirement.mind: The colossus can direct itself if necessary.
eberron.rule.colossus-crew-requirement.who_may: Crew meeting the specified roles and marks.
eberron.rule.colossus-crew-requirement.combines: Crew operates the docent network and weapons.
eberron.rule.colossus-crew-requirement.blocked_reason: This is a direct operational restriction.

eberron.rule.docent-network-creation-los.name: Docent network creation loss

effect.summary: The techniques and tools for making docent nodes were lost in the Mourning.

eberron.rule.docent-network-creation-los.cost_or_limit: New node production cannot use the lost techniques and tools.
eberron.rule.docent-network-creation-los.combines: Cannith seeks to salvage existing networks.
eberron.rule.docent-network-creation-los.blocked_reason: This is a direct restriction on producing an item.

eberron.rule.emerald-claw-dissolution.name: Emerald Claw dissolution

effect.summary: King Kaius III disbanded the orders and condemned many Emerald Claw members as war criminals.

eberron.rule.emerald-claw-dissolution.cost_or_limit: The order was required to disband; rebellious members refused.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-dissolution.go_wrong: The order fragmented into independent cells.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-dissolution.where_from: Karrnath near the end of the Last War.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-dissolution.combines: Some members continued under Lady Illmarrow.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-dissolution.blocked_reason: This is a direct world-history restriction.

eberron.rule.colossus-power-core-contain.name: Colossus power-core containment

effect.summary: A specifically cut large Khyber shard can contain raw magical energy without exploding.

eberron.rule.colossus-power-core-contain.cost_or_limit: The shard must be cut to a particular pattern.
eberron.rule.colossus-power-core-contain.go_wrong: Without the correct pattern, it may explode.
eberron.rule.colossus-power-core-contain.combines: The shard is connected to a harness that distributes energy.
eberron.rule.colossus-power-core-contain.blocked_reason: The rule depends on an item’s capacity to contain dangerous energy.

eberron.rule.colossus-dead-man-defense.name: Colossus dead-man defense

effect.summary: If the operator alerts, leaves, or dies, the master docent seals doors and activates defenses in attacked areas.

eberron.rule.colossus-dead-man-defense.cost_or_limit: Defenses remain inactive while the operator is connected and in control.
eberron.rule.colossus-dead-man-defense.go_wrong: Doors seal and wards and traps arm when control is lost.
eberron.rule.colossus-dead-man-defense.combines: Uses network, door seals, wards, and traps.
eberron.rule.colossus-dead-man-defense.blocked_reason: The rule activates multiple area defenses across a large structure.

eberron.rule.colossus-bound-elemental-we.name: Colossus bound-elemental weapon control

effect.summary: Elementals supply colossus attacks and defenses, directed through the docent network.

eberron.rule.colossus-bound-elemental-we.cost_or_limit: Optimal use relies on a weapons officer with the Mark of Storm.
eberron.rule.colossus-bound-elemental-we.go_wrong: Broken binding shards may free the elemental.
eberron.rule.colossus-bound-elemental-we.who_may: Captain and weapons officer operate the weapons.
eberron.rule.colossus-bound-elemental-we.combines: Docent network, bound elementals, and marked operator.
eberron.rule.colossus-bound-elemental-we.blocked_reason: The mechanism binds an independent being to equipment and permits its release.

eberron.rule.emerald-claw-afterlife-prom.name: Emerald Claw afterlife promise

effect.summary: Followers expect Illmarrow’s ascension to grant immortality or eternal undeath.

eberron.rule.emerald-claw-afterlife-prom.cost_or_limit: Depends on Illmarrow becoming a god of death.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-afterlife-prom.go_wrong: The promise is a belief and may not be fulfilled.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-afterlife-prom.mind: Followers are motivated by promised power or eternal life.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-afterlife-prom.who_may: Emerald Claw members who believe the claim.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-afterlife-prom.where_from: The order’s beliefs about Lady Illmarrow.
eberron.rule.emerald-claw-afterlife-prom.blocked_reason: Immortality and undeath concern lifespan and post-death state.

eberron.rule.plane-influence-waxes-and-w.name: Plane influence waxes and wanes

effect.summary: Planar influence shifts in strength; strong influence is coterminous and weak influence is remote.

eberron.rule.plane-influence-waxes-and-w.cost_or_limit: The timing depends on the story.
eberron.rule.plane-influence-waxes-and-w.who_may: Affects planar interactions and linked sites.
eberron.rule.plane-influence-waxes-and-w.combines: Can matter for rituals, eldritch machines, and extraplanar interaction.
eberron.rule.plane-influence-waxes-and-w.blocked_reason: The state of a plane changes effects across linked locations.

eberron.rule.manifest-zones-have-plane-s.name: Manifest zones have plane-shaped properties

effect.summary: Thin boundaries let linked-plane characteristics bleed into Material Plane locations.

eberron.rule.manifest-zones-have-plane-s.cost_or_limit: Most effects persist; weak links may act only when the plane is coterminous.
eberron.rule.manifest-zones-have-plane-s.go_wrong: Weak links may not operate consistently.
eberron.rule.manifest-zones-have-plane-s.who_may: Creatures and sites within a manifest zone.
eberron.rule.manifest-zones-have-plane-s.where_from: Planar overlap with the Material Plane.
eberron.rule.manifest-zones-have-plane-s.combines: A zone may include a portal between planes.
eberron.rule.manifest-zones-have-plane-s.blocked_reason: Persistent and conditional location-wide effects need area-field rules.

eberron.rule.dal-quor-is-always-remote.name: Dal Quor is always remote

effect.summary: The plane cannot form manifest zones with the Material Plane.

eberron.rule.dal-quor-is-always-remote.cost_or_limit: Dreaming psychic projection is the only stated way to reach it.
eberron.rule.dal-quor-is-always-remote.go_wrong: Quori must possess mortal hosts to act on Eberron.
eberron.rule.dal-quor-is-always-remote.mind: Dreaming is the means of contact.
eberron.rule.dal-quor-is-always-remote.where_from: The severed connection between Dal Quor and Eberron.
eberron.rule.dal-quor-is-always-remote.combines: Quori use dream projection and possession.
eberron.rule.dal-quor-is-always-remote.blocked_reason: The exceptional dream route and denied planar connection require spatial and psychic access rules.

eberron.rule.a-dead-mortal-soul-is-drawn.name: A dead mortal soul is drawn to Dolurrh

effect.summary: A mortal soul goes to Dolurrh after death and gradually loses memory.

eberron.rule.a-dead-mortal-soul-is-drawn.cost_or_limit: The destination beyond Dolurrh is uncertain in the passage.
eberron.rule.a-dead-mortal-soul-is-drawn.go_wrong: The soul may appear to dissolve into a husk.
eberron.rule.a-dead-mortal-soul-is-drawn.combines: Religions interpret Dolurrh as a gateway to further existence.
eberron.rule.a-dead-mortal-soul-is-drawn.blocked_reason: After-death travel and ongoing soul alteration need soul-state rules.

eberron.rule.plane-state-depends-on-the-.name: Plane state depends on the story

effect.summary: The story determines when a plane is remote or coterminous.

eberron.rule.plane-state-depends-on-the-.combines: Affects rituals, machines, and extraplanar interaction.
eberron.rule.plane-state-depends-on-the-.blocked_reason: The passage assigns the timing to the story rather than specifying a mechanical effect.

eberron.rule.eberron-is-secluded-from-th.name: Eberron is secluded from the wider multiverse

effect.summary: Its cosmology is designed to prevent outside planar travel and influence.

eberron.rule.eberron-is-secluded-from-th.cost_or_limit: Campaigns may instead allow contact if the Ring of Siberys weakens.
eberron.rule.eberron-is-secluded-from-th.go_wrong: A weakening barrier could permit outsiders to interfere.
eberron.rule.eberron-is-secluded-from-th.who_may: Restricts outside gods, celestials, and fiends.
eberron.rule.eberron-is-secluded-from-th.combines: Associated with the Deep Ethereal, planar spells, and Ring of Siberys.
eberron.rule.eberron-is-secluded-from-th.blocked_reason: World-scale isolation and conditional access need containment mechanics.

eberron.rule.the-ring-of-siberys-can-be-.name: The Ring of Siberys can be intact or weakening

effect.summary: A weakened barrier can permit limited contact with outside worlds.

eberron.rule.the-ring-of-siberys-can-be-.cost_or_limit: Contact may be recent and limited.
eberron.rule.the-ring-of-siberys-can-be-.go_wrong: Outside powers may begin meddling in Eberron.
eberron.rule.the-ring-of-siberys-can-be-.who_may: The campaign determines the barrier’s state.
eberron.rule.the-ring-of-siberys-can-be-.where_from: The default assumption is that the barrier is intact.
eberron.rule.the-ring-of-siberys-can-be-.combines: Its weakening may be linked to the Mourning.
eberron.rule.the-ring-of-siberys-can-be-.blocked_reason: A changing cosmological barrier and its access consequences require containment rules.

eberron.rule.a-newly-arrived-outsider-ha.name: A newly arrived outsider has no established local lore or power base

effect.summary: If an outside power is newly discovered, Eberron lacks its history and established followers.

eberron.rule.a-newly-arrived-outsider-ha.cost_or_limit: Applies when contact is recent and limited.
eberron.rule.a-newly-arrived-outsider-ha.go_wrong: The outsider must recruit followers and alliances may form against it.
eberron.rule.a-newly-arrived-outsider-ha.who_may: Eberron’s inhabitants and newly arrived outsiders.
eberron.rule.a-newly-arrived-outsider-ha.where_from: The consequences of recent multiversal contact.
eberron.rule.a-newly-arrived-outsider-ha.combines: May prompt unusual alliances between celestials and fiends.
eberron.rule.a-newly-arrived-outsider-ha.blocked_reason: The passage gives a setting consequence rather than a supernatural effect.

eberron.rule.eberron-s-gods-do-not-usual.name: Eberron’s gods do not usually physically intervene

effect.summary: Faithful people attribute triumphs to divine influence but do not expect gods to appear and solve problems.

eberron.rule.eberron-s-gods-do-not-usual.cost_or_limit: This describes the usual religious outlook.
eberron.rule.eberron-s-gods-do-not-usual.mind: The faithful interpret events through belief.
eberron.rule.eberron-s-gods-do-not-usual.combines: Contrasts faith with concrete divine action.
eberron.rule.eberron-s-gods-do-not-usual.blocked_reason: This is a setting expectation, not a game effect.

eberron.rule.couatl-souls-formed-a-priso.name: Couatl souls formed a prison for the overlords

effect.summary: The couatls combined their souls to imprison the ancient fiendish overlords.

eberron.rule.couatl-souls-formed-a-priso.go_wrong: The souls’ ultimate fate is uncertain, though some theorize they became the Silver Flame’s force.
eberron.rule.couatl-souls-formed-a-priso.mind: The passage does not specify the souls’ awareness.
eberron.rule.couatl-souls-formed-a-priso.combines: The prison is connected in theory to the Church of the Silver Flame.
eberron.rule.couatl-souls-formed-a-priso.blocked_reason: Soul combination and an enduring prison binding need soul-state and containment mechanics.

eberron.rule.a-fiend-may-be-khyber-spawn.name: A fiend may be Khyber-spawned, bound, or independent

effect.summary: Khyber can spawn any kind of fiend; it may serve an overlord or act independently.

eberron.rule.a-fiend-may-be-khyber-spawn.go_wrong: Independent fiends may be unleashed on the world.
eberron.rule.a-fiend-may-be-khyber-spawn.combines: May be bound to an overlord or be an independent incarnation of evil.
eberron.rule.a-fiend-may-be-khyber-spawn.blocked_reason: This is a setting rule about origin and allegiance, not a supernatural effect.

eberron.rule.many-rakshasas-serve-or-see.name: Many rakshasas serve or seek the overlords’ power

effect.summary: Rakshasas in the Lords of Dust may pursue different aims concerning their imprisoned masters.

eberron.rule.many-rakshasas-serve-or-see.cost_or_limit: Some want to free overlords; others seek their power.
eberron.rule.many-rakshasas-serve-or-see.go_wrong: Their schemes take place in the shadows.
eberron.rule.many-rakshasas-serve-or-see.mind: They scheme toward their own goals.
eberron.rule.many-rakshasas-serve-or-see.who_may: Rakshasas of the Lords of Dust.
eberron.rule.many-rakshasas-serve-or-see.blocked_reason: The passage describes motives rather than a special game effect.

eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-constructi.name: Elemental vessel construction requirements

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-constructi.cost_or_limit: A large, fine Khyber shard binds the elemental; a Siberys shard crafts the helm; construction requires many workers and months.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-constructi.go_wrong: Production halts without a steady supply of both shard types.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-constructi.who_may: Workshops with specialized expertise and labor.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-constructi.combines: Dragonshards, engineering, arcane skill, rare materials, and a workshop.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-constructi.blocked_reason: This is a resource and production restriction.

eberron.rule.elemental-matrix-operation.name: Elemental matrix operation

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.elemental-matrix-operation.cost_or_limit: The bound elemental must be placed in the containment chamber for the matrix to activate.
eberron.rule.elemental-matrix-operation.go_wrong: Suppressing the elemental returns it to the chamber and stops propulsion.
eberron.rule.elemental-matrix-operation.who_may: A dragonmarked pilot can command suppression.
eberron.rule.elemental-matrix-operation.combines: Containment chamber, binding struts, hull, and bound elemental.
eberron.rule.elemental-matrix-operation.mechanism: Arcane matrix channels an elemental through the vehicle.
eberron.rule.elemental-matrix-operation.blocked_reason: The matrix depends on a contained entity and its release into the vehicle’s workings.

eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-control.name: Elemental vessel control

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-control.cost_or_limit: A dragonmarked heir commands easily; another character touching the Khyber shard or helm can attempt a DC 20 Charisma check, with success lasting one minute.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-control.go_wrong: Without control or suppression, the elemental moves the vessel by whim.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-control.mind: The elemental can be persuaded or intimidated into obedience.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-control.who_may: A dragonmarked heir, or a character who touches the shard or helm and succeeds at the check.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-control.combines: The dominate monster and charm monster spells can affect control.
eberron.rule.elemental-vessel-control.blocked_reason: The rule includes persuasion, obedience, and magical control of a creature.

eberron.rule.freeing-the-elemental.name: Freeing the elemental

effect.summary: Breaking the Khyber shard frees the elemental and prevents the vehicle from moving.

eberron.rule.freeing-the-elemental.cost_or_limit: The shard has AC 17 and 10 hit points; it is usually protected by a chest and sometimes wards and locked or trapped doors.
eberron.rule.freeing-the-elemental.go_wrong: The vehicle loses propulsion when the elemental is freed.
eberron.rule.freeing-the-elemental.who_may: Anyone able to break the binding shard.
eberron.rule.freeing-the-elemental.combines: The shard is commonly secured in a protective metal chest.
eberron.rule.freeing-the-elemental.mechanism: Destroying a binding object releases its captive.
eberron.rule.freeing-the-elemental.blocked_reason: The effect depends on a binding and release mechanism for an elemental.

eberron.rule.airship-operating-limits.name: Airship operating limits

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.airship-operating-limits.cost_or_limit: A Mark of Storm heir pilots; at least two pilots usually travel; the vessel reaches about 20 miles per hour, carries up to 30 tons, and cannot land.
eberron.rule.airship-operating-limits.go_wrong: Unusual maneuvers risk passengers and crew.
eberron.rule.airship-operating-limits.who_may: House Lyrandar Mark of Storm heirs.
eberron.rule.airship-operating-limits.combines: Wheel, bound elemental, and buoyant soarwood hull.
eberron.rule.airship-operating-limits.blocked_reason: The propulsion limitation depends on the elemental-binding mechanism.

eberron.rule.lightning-rail-operating-li.name: Lightning rail operating limits

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.lightning-rail-operating-li.cost_or_limit: The route follows conductor stones, and House Orien rules forbid stopping except at stations.
eberron.rule.lightning-rail-operating-li.go_wrong: The pilot can select the wrong branch at a junction.
eberron.rule.lightning-rail-operating-li.who_may: House Orien pilots operate the train.
eberron.rule.lightning-rail-operating-li.blocked_reason: The restrictions are straightforward movement limits.

eberron.rule.house-orien-station-stoppin.name: House Orien station stopping rule

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.house-orien-station-stoppin.cost_or_limit: Lightning rail pilots are prohibited from stopping anywhere except a station.
eberron.rule.house-orien-station-stoppin.who_may: Lightning rail pilots are subject to the restriction.
eberron.rule.house-orien-station-stoppin.combines: Applies to the lightning rail route.
eberron.rule.house-orien-station-stoppin.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward rule restriction.

eberron.rule.sharn-heights-bridge-spacin.name: Sharn Heights bridge spacing

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.sharn-heights-bridge-spacin.cost_or_limit: Each bridge is about 20 feet higher than the one directly below it.
eberron.rule.sharn-heights-bridge-spacin.go_wrong: Falls from the bridges can be deadly.
eberron.rule.sharn-heights-bridge-spacin.who_may: Applies to users of the location.
eberron.rule.sharn-heights-bridge-spacin.combines: Bridges and platforms intersect throughout the heights.

eberron.rule.dreamlily-medicinal-legalit.name: Dreamlily medicinal legality and taxation

effect.summary: Dreamlily is legal for medicinal use but heavily taxed, encouraging black-market smuggling.

eberron.rule.dreamlily-medicinal-legalit.cost_or_limit: Medicinal use is legal; the substance is heavily taxed.
eberron.rule.dreamlily-medicinal-legalit.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward world rule about legality and taxation.

eberron.rule.dreamlily-s-first-drop-to-0.name: Dreamlily’s first drop to 0 hit points

effect.summary: The first time the user would reach 0 hit points without being killed outright, they remain at 1 hit point.

eberron.rule.dreamlily-s-first-drop-to-0.cost_or_limit: Applies only the first time during the drug’s effect.
eberron.rule.dreamlily-s-first-drop-to-0.go_wrong: The user is poisoned for one hour by the drug.
eberron.rule.dreamlily-s-first-drop-to-0.combines: Occurs alongside fear immunity while poisoned.
eberron.rule.dreamlily-s-first-drop-to-0.blocked_reason: A triggered vitality change can be represented by the basic effect grammar.

eberron.rule.dragon-s-blood-unpredictabi.name: Dragon’s blood unpredictability

effect.summary: The drug’s effects are intentionally unpredictable and may produce dangerous outcomes.

eberron.rule.dragon-s-blood-unpredictabi.go_wrong: Effects may be unpredictable and harmful.
eberron.rule.dragon-s-blood-unpredictabi.blocked_reason: The passage leaves the drug’s unpredictable outcomes to the game master rather than defining a specific effect.

eberron.rule.dragonshard-dust-as-spell-c.name: Dragonshard dust as spell components

effect.summary: Eberron dragonshard dust can substitute for a priced spell component at equivalent market value, unless the DM rules otherwise.

eberron.rule.dragonshard-dust-as-spell-c.cost_or_limit: Must match the replaced component’s market value.
eberron.rule.dragonshard-dust-as-spell-c.combines: Can fuel almost any act of magic and is used in some magic-item creation
eberron.rule.dragonshard-dust-as-spell-c.blocked_reason: This is a resource exchange rule that can be implemented directly.

eberron.rule.ongoing-dragonshard-mainten.name: Ongoing dragonshard maintenance

effect.summary: Some powerful tools must continually consume Eberron dragonshards to keep their enchantments working.

eberron.rule.ongoing-dragonshard-mainten.cost_or_limit: Requires a continuing expenditure of dragonshards.
eberron.rule.ongoing-dragonshard-mainten.go_wrong: Enchantment maintenance cannot continue without the required expenditure.
eberron.rule.ongoing-dragonshard-mainten.who_may: Operators or maintainers of the tools
eberron.rule.ongoing-dragonshard-mainten.combines: Applies to the lightning rail and elemental airships
eberron.rule.ongoing-dragonshard-mainten.blocked_reason: The ongoing cost can be represented as a recurring resource requirement.

eberron.rule.elemental-binding-containme.name: Elemental binding containment

effect.summary: Elemental binding requires a Khyber dragonshard to hold the bound elemental.

eberron.rule.elemental-binding-containme.cost_or_limit: Requires a Khyber dragonshard as a vessel.
eberron.rule.elemental-binding-containme.combines: Used in airships, lightning rail, and elemental galleons
eberron.rule.elemental-binding-containme.blocked_reason: The rule requires a specific vessel that holds a bound elemental.

eberron.rule.eldritch-machines-need-spec.name: Eldritch machines need special conditions

effect.summary: Powerful machines need special components and conditions, sometimes including a suitable manifest zone.

eberron.rule.eldritch-machines-need-spec.cost_or_limit: Operation may depend on components or planar conditions.
eberron.rule.eldritch-machines-need-spec.blocked_reason: This is a general operational constraint, not an unrepresentable effect.

eberron.rule.common-magic-item-availabil.name: Common magic item availability

effect.summary: Common magic items are widely sold, with stock and search outcomes determined locally.

eberron.rule.common-magic-item-availabil.cost_or_limit: Search difficulty varies by settlement; a failed search requires waiting at least 24 hours before trying for the same item there.
eberron.rule.common-magic-item-availabil.combines: Search DC is 10 in a city, 15 in a town, and 20 in a village.

eberron.rule.common-magic-item-prices.name: Common magic item prices

effect.summary: The DM sets common-item prices or rolls 2d4 × 10 gp, halved for consumables.

eberron.rule.common-magic-item-prices.cost_or_limit: Consumables cost half the rolled price.

eberron.rule.dragonshard-crafting-requir.name: Dragonshard crafting requirements

effect.summary: A dragonshard can ease creation of a common magic item if the crafter has suitable tool or Arcana proficiency.

eberron.rule.dragonshard-crafting-requir.cost_or_limit: The shard is consumed; spell scrolls require a spell known and its material components; a cantrip scroll works as if cast by a first-level caster.
eberron.rule.dragonshard-crafting-requir.who_may: A character with relevant tool proficiency or Arcana proficiency; scroll scribers must know the spell.
eberron.rule.dragonshard-crafting-requir.combines: Crafting time and cost depend on item type.
eberron.rule.dragonshard-crafting-requir.blocked_reason: The rule specifies straightforward crafting requirements and costs.

eberron.rule.crafting-complication-chanc.name: Crafting complication chance

effect.summary: Noncommon item crafting has a 10 percent chance of complications for each five workweeks spent.

eberron.rule.crafting-complication-chanc.cost_or_limit: Each five workweeks adds a 10 percent chance.
eberron.rule.crafting-complication-chanc.go_wrong: Possible complications include political attention, a temporary manifest zone, missing components, planar delay, faction interest, or sentience.
eberron.rule.crafting-complication-chanc.combines: Planar delays last 2d6 days; complications can be rolled or selected.
eberron.rule.crafting-complication-chanc.blocked_reason: This is a probability rule for crafting complications.

eberron.rule.daelkyr-domain-passages.name: Daelkyr domain passages

effect.summary: Passing through a daelkyr domain can connect distant surface locations and shorten travel.

eberron.rule.daelkyr-domain-passages.cost_or_limit: Passages are found in tunnels and chasms; geography within the demiplanes is unconventional.
eberron.rule.daelkyr-domain-passages.go_wrong: Travel routes may defy ordinary geography.
eberron.rule.daelkyr-domain-passages.blocked_reason: Travel through connected demiplane spaces is not represented by the basic effect grammar.

eberron.rule.quori-vessel-benefits.name: Quori vessel benefits

effect.summary: A possessing quori grants benefits according to its type while using the host’s knowledge and features.

eberron.rule.quori-vessel-benefits.cost_or_limit: Benefits depend on whether the spirit is Hashalaq, Kalaraq, or Tsucora.
eberron.rule.quori-vessel-benefits.mind: The quori accesses the vessel’s knowledge.
eberron.rule.quori-vessel-benefits.who_may: Inspired vessels and their possessing quori.
eberron.rule.quori-vessel-benefits.combines: Hashalaq grants Suggestion; Kalaraq grants All Around Vision and Arcane Eye; Tsucora grants Fear.
eberron.rule.quori-vessel-benefits.blocked_reason: The rule depends on a possessing spirit bound to a host.

eberron.rule.odakyr-rites.name: Odakyr Rites

effect.summary: Grants Karrnathi undead tactical judgment and the ability to act without direct guidance.

eberron.rule.odakyr-rites.cost_or_limit: Works only on remains of soldiers slain in battle and only in Mabar manifest zones.
eberron.rule.odakyr-rites.go_wrong: Some fear the undead may serve a darker power or turn against the living.
eberron.rule.odakyr-rites.mind: Grants intelligence for independent tactical decisions.
eberron.rule.odakyr-rites.where_from: Developed by Malevanor with Blood of Vol priests.
eberron.rule.odakyr-rites.combines: Requires suitable remains and a Mabar manifest zone.

eberron.rule.illmarrow-s-rejuvenation.name: Illmarrow’s rejuvenation

effect.summary: After destruction, Illmarrow’s body reforms within two hundred miles after 1d10 days.

eberron.rule.illmarrow-s-rejuvenation.cost_or_limit: Her hidden phylactery enables the return and determines a random safe haven.
eberron.rule.illmarrow-s-rejuvenation.go_wrong: Her equipment remains behind when her body turns to dust.
eberron.rule.illmarrow-s-rejuvenation.mind: Illmarrow herself does not know the phylactery’s location or form.
eberron.rule.illmarrow-s-rejuvenation.where_from: Minara Vol’s enchantments on the phylactery.
eberron.rule.illmarrow-s-rejuvenation.combines: The effect follows destruction and return in a new body.
eberron.rule.illmarrow-s-rejuvenation.blocked_reason: It requires a death-and-return state tied to a phylactery.

eberron.rule.mabar-manifest-zone-restric.name: Mabar manifest-zone restriction

effect.summary: The Odakyr Rites work only in manifest zones tied to Mabar.

eberron.rule.mabar-manifest-zone-restric.cost_or_limit: Also requires the remains of a soldier slain in battle.
eberron.rule.mabar-manifest-zone-restric.go_wrong: The rites do not work outside these conditions.
eberron.rule.mabar-manifest-zone-restric.where_from: Karrnath’s Mabar manifest zones, especially Atur and Odakyr.
eberron.rule.mabar-manifest-zone-restric.combines: Works together with suitable battle-slain remains.

eberron.rule.living-spell-customization.name: Living spell customization

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.living-spell-customization.cost_or_limit: Choose a damage-dealing evocation or conjuration wizard spell of level 5 or lower; levels 1–2 use Living burning hands, 3–4 Living lightning bolt, and level 5 Living cloudkill as the base.
eberron.rule.living-spell-customization.combines: Chosen spell determines damage immunity, strike damage, and mimicry effect.
eberron.rule.living-spell-customization.blocked_reason: This is a construction procedure, not a supernatural effect.

eberron.rule.warforged-nature.name: Warforged Nature

effect.summary: none

eberron.rule.warforged-nature.cost_or_limit: The Lord of Blades requires no air, food, drink, or sleep.
eberron.rule.warforged-nature.who_may: Warforged, as described for the Lord of Blades.
eberron.rule.warforged-nature.blocked_reason: This is a world rule about sustenance requirements.

eberron.rule.silver-flame-binding.name: Silver Flame binding

effect.summary: Celestial light holds the undestroyable overlords imprisoned in Khyber and prevents physical manifestation.

eberron.rule.silver-flame-binding.cost_or_limit: The binding can weaken as overlords gain strength and influence.
eberron.rule.silver-flame-binding.go_wrong: If the bonds fail, overlords may return to the world.
eberron.rule.silver-flame-binding.who_may: Overlords are bound; the couatl created the prison.
eberron.rule.silver-flame-binding.combines: Rak Tulkhesh's soul is additionally divided among Khyber shards.
eberron.rule.silver-flame-binding.blocked_reason: The rule depends on persistent binding and a barrier to physical manifestation.

eberron.rule.immortal-nature.name: Immortal Nature

effect.summary: An overlord that dies reforms elsewhere in the multiverse and becomes active again when the DM decides.

eberron.rule.immortal-nature.combines: They also require no air, food, drink, or sleep.
eberron.rule.immortal-nature.blocked_reason: The rule requires persistent identity and a return after death.

eberron.rule.arcane-cataclysm-field-exce.name: Arcane Cataclysm field exception

effect.summary: Each burst area suppresses magic for one hour, except Sul Khatesh and her spells.

eberron.rule.arcane-cataclysm-field-exce.cost_or_limit: The exception applies to Sul Khatesh and spells she casts.
eberron.rule.arcane-cataclysm-field-exce.blocked_reason: It suppresses other magical effects while exempting a specific source.

eberron.rule.magewright-ritual-component.name: Magewright ritual components

effect.summary: A magewright's ritual uses extra materials worth 20 gold pieces per spell level, consumed when the ritual ends.

eberron.rule.magewright-ritual-component.cost_or_limit: Cost is 20 gp per spell level, and components are consumed.
eberron.rule.magewright-ritual-component.combines: Applies to ritual spells in the magewright stat block.
eberron.rule.magewright-ritual-component.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward resource cost and consumption rule.

eberron.rule.positive-energy-sustains-un.name: Positive energy sustains undying

effect.summary: Positive energy or mortal devotion keeps an undying spirit going; without it, the spirit fades and dies.

eberron.rule.positive-energy-sustains-un.cost_or_limit: Devotion is finite; an undying elf outside Aerenal needs a community or another source of positive energy.
eberron.rule.positive-energy-sustains-un.go_wrong: The undying's light fades and it eventually dies.
eberron.rule.positive-energy-sustains-un.where_from: Irian-linked manifest zones or mortal devotion.
eberron.rule.positive-energy-sustains-un.combines: The Undying Court's worship sustains Aerenal's undying.
eberron.rule.positive-energy-sustains-un.blocked_reason: The rule governs continued existence and death of a spirit.

eberron.rule.undying-body-and-spirit.name: Undying body and spirit

effect.summary: Irian's light sustains the spirit but does not preserve the body, which dries out over centuries.

eberron.rule.undying-body-and-spirit.cost_or_limit: The body withers while the spirit persists; the most powerful can separate spirit from body.
eberron.rule.undying-body-and-spirit.go_wrong: The spirit eventually dies if its sustaining source fails.
eberron.rule.undying-body-and-spirit.combines: Some councilors can become beings of pure light.
eberron.rule.undying-body-and-spirit.mechanism: Separate body and spirit; spirit sustenance
eberron.rule.undying-body-and-spirit.blocked_reason: The rule distinguishes a living spirit from a decaying body and permits spirit-body separation.

eberron.rule.radiant-idols-need-no-food-.name: Radiant idols need no food, drink, or sleep

effect.summary: A radiant idol has no need for food, drink, or sleep.

eberron.rule.radiant-idols-need-no-food-.cost_or_limit: No food, drink, or sleep required.
eberron.rule.radiant-idols-need-no-food-.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward restriction on ordinary survival needs.

eberron.rule.undying-require-no-air-food.name: Undying require no air, food, drink, or sleep

effect.summary: An undying does not require air, food, drink, or sleep.

eberron.rule.undying-require-no-air-food.combines: Does not eliminate the need for positive energy or devotion.
eberron.rule.undying-require-no-air-food.blocked_reason: The creature has no ordinary bodily needs but its spirit still requires supernatural sustenance.

eberron.rule.warforged-colossus-interior.name: Warforged Colossus interior

effect.summary: A colossus is hollow inside, with passages and spaces for crew and cargo, and can operate without a crew.

eberron.rule.warforged-colossus-interior.cost_or_limit: Built to carry wizards, artificers, magewrights, and elite troops.
eberron.rule.warforged-colossus-interior.go_wrong: It may contain monsters, secrets, and corpses.
eberron.rule.warforged-colossus-interior.combines: Can serve as an adventure site.
eberron.rule.warforged-colossus-interior.blocked_reason: The rule describes interior storage and traversable spaces within a construct.

eberron.rule.bonecraft-armor-binding.name: Bonecraft armor binding

effect.summary: A bone knight's armor cannot be removed without killing its wearer.

eberron.rule.bonecraft-armor-binding.cost_or_limit: Removing the armor kills the knight.
eberron.rule.bonecraft-armor-binding.go_wrong: The wearer dies if separated from the armor.
eberron.rule.bonecraft-armor-binding.mind: The wearer accepts that their former life is over.
eberron.rule.bonecraft-armor-binding.combines: Armor focuses the knight's divine gifts.
eberron.rule.bonecraft-armor-binding.blocked_reason: The wearer's life and abilities are inseparably linked to an item, with lethal removal.

eberron.rule.magewright-rituals-take-ext.name: Magewright rituals take extra time

effect.summary: Most magewright rituals take ten minutes, while complex rituals may take as long as an hour.

eberron.rule.magewright-rituals-take-ext.cost_or_limit: Ten minutes typically; up to one hour for complex rituals.
eberron.rule.magewright-rituals-take-ext.combines: Rituals also require extra material components.
eberron.rule.magewright-rituals-take-ext.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward time cost.
